source.title: Ada2MS: A Hybrid Optimization Algorithm Based on Exponential Mixing of Elementwise and Global Second-Moment Estimates
source.authors: Meng Zhu; Quan Xiao; Wei-Dong Min

page_placements.theme: Optimizer design and tuning affect held-out rankings

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied; no apparent truncation or garbling affecting the reported results.
record.tranche_reason: Compares adaptive and momentum optimizers on held-out benchmark metrics under a shared protocol, bearing on the optimizer and generalization relationship in V4.
record.gate_note: The paper's results compare optimizers on three visual tasks. Rows below record AdamW and RAdam against momentum SGD; results for the proposed Ada2MS and other optimizers are not rows because they do not directly measure the adaptive-versus-momentum comparison named in V4. Cited prior-work results are not included.
record.test_reason: The CIFAR-100 experiment directly compares adaptive optimizers with momentum SGD on held-out classification error, bearing on V4. Detection and segmentation measure tasks outside V4's stated classification and language scope.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that Ada2MS is competitive on CIFAR-100 and best among the compared optimizers on VOC detection under their protocol, while calling for more hybrid baselines, switching-schedule ablations, and nonvisual validation.
record.recipe_differences: The study compares several optimizers under its own unified protocol and proposes Ada2MS; it does not reproduce the original studies' full benchmark and tuning protocols. It reports peak learning rates, a shared warmup and minimum-rate rule, and weight-decay settings, but not broad optimizer hyperparameter sweeps.
record.method_sensitivity: Task and model change the relative results: AdamW outperforms Momentum SGD on SwinV2-S and YOLOv7-tiny, while Momentum SGD slightly outperforms AdamW on U-Net. RAdam's ordering also varies by task.

fits_no_version.finding: On VOC detection, AdamW and RAdam reach 59.12% and 58.89% mAP@0.5 versus momentum SGD's 57.19%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Adaptive optimizers can outperform momentum SGD on held-out object detection under a prescribed training recipe.

fits_no_version.finding: On Semantic Boundaries segmentation, momentum SGD reaches 52.40% mIoU, AdamW 52.28%, and RAdam 52.83%, without reported uncertainty.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Adaptive-versus-momentum optimizer ordering on semantic segmentation depends on the optimizer and training recipe.

record.problems: The authors describe the protocol as a relatively fair comparison but acknowledge that more hybrid baselines and more complete switching-schedule ablations are needed. No uncertainty estimates are reported. The experiments cover visual tasks only.
record.rows_left_out: No directly relevant AdamW or RAdam versus Momentum SGD comparison rows left out. Results for Ada2MS and other optimizers in Tables 3–5 were omitted because they do not directly measure the adaptive-versus-momentum comparison named in V4.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its coexistence with natural-label generalization.
Width variation beyond the width needed for interpolation.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and local connectivity.

Language benchmarks; broader tuning versus limited tuning; causal effects of decoupling weight decay or switching to SGD; comparisons at equal or better training performance. AdamW is evaluated, but decoupled weight decay is not isolated experimentally.
Batch-size effects and remedies under matched epoch budgets.
Dropout effects and joint removal of dropout and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its association with generalization gaps. Update-norm stability analysis does not measure this relationship.
Removal of memorized training examples and subsequent test accuracy.

missing.what: CIFAR-100 Top-5 error comparisons: momentum SGD 10.73%, AdamW 8.39%, and RAdam 8.37%. These corroborate the Top-1 ordering but have no rows and are not declared omitted.

record.verdict_notes: No uncertainty estimates or training-performance comparisons are supplied. Prescribed parameter alignment does not establish a matched tuning budget. The study is not an original source. Results explicitly declared omitted are not listed as missing; however, excluding all other optimizers categorically is too restrictive because adaptive baselines such as SophiaG can also bear on V4.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and generalization on natural labels.
Network width beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and local connectivity.
Language benchmarks; broader hyperparameter tuning; decoupled weight decay or switching from Adam to SGD; word-level language models; explicit comparisons under equal or better training performance.
Removing memorized examples and measuring test accuracy.

relationships.condition: SwinV2-S trained from scratch on CIFAR-100 for 160 epochs using WSDS and the prescribed optimizer parameter alignment
relationships.reason: R1–R3 show AdamW and RAdam at 29.38% Top-1 error versus momentum SGD at 33.22%; this qualifies the adaptive-method disadvantage for this recipe, while AdamW's success is compatible with V4's decoupled-weight-decay qualification.
relationships.display_finding: AdamW and RAdam achieved 29.38% Top-1 error versus momentum SGD's 33.22%, with repeated-run uncertainty unreported.
